parsed.explanation: The combined regime criminalises gender nonconformity and transition itself through 'indecent acts' (up to five years) and 'illicit intercourse' provisions, with religious rulings narrowing the ground for care — a state-level, traveller-facing criminal exposure for anyone outed or outable. No discrimination protections, no legal gender recognition, and no LGBTI organisational infrastructure remove recourse. Organised militia killings, torture and targeting for effeminate dress are documented, but are dated (2012–2015), territorial, and channelled outside the courts, so they weigh as a serious but not currently measured layer rather than a universal state campaign. No execution pathway for gender expression is documented. Net: imprisonment credible on discovery, no working remedy, plus residual territorial violence risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Presentation-document mismatch has no domestic remedy; legal gender recognition unavailable and identity documents cannot be changed, leaving outed visitors exposed to morality-offence enforcement.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch escalates from screening into the indecent-acts/illicit-intercourse provisions, converting a document query into criminal exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: De-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and the transition process, enforced through morality provisions carrying up to five years' imprisonment; militia torture of detainees documented in an earlier period.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented protection; no named statute carve-out and no record of relief for gender-nonconforming detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Armed-group territorial control creates a second, non-judicial custody route distinct from the penal code.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Geographic axis of armed-group control documented; killings of men accused of homosexuality, including one for effeminate dress, occurred in militia-held territory.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Territory of stay determines whether exposure is the national morality offence or militia enforcement; reporting from the named city was mosque-only and incomplete.

care_services.exposure: Recent religious rulings designate gender-affirming medical steps impermissible, narrowing care access; no discrimination protections apply to clinics.
care_services.interaction: A traveller seeking or carrying transition-related care risks being seen to have undergone impermissible steps, feeding the same morality provisions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Gender nonconformity and transition itself framed as criminal/de-facto illicit; no legal protections against SOGI discrimination; LGBTI organisations cannot register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing aligns with religious rulings, so institutions and moral authority reinforce rather than check each other.

minors_guardians.exposure: A parent travelling with a minor risks exposure through the same morality provisions; the dossier records a 2010 case of a girl jailed, raped and forced into marriage after online disclosure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Child-inclusive discovery compounds adult exposure, with no registered support infrastructure to intervene.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented militia executions, torture of twelve men, and targeting for effeminate dress (2012–2015); situation reported as worsening under militia control.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; reporting incomplete and information in the named city flowed only through the mosque.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street-level hostility runs through militia/extremist channels rather than courts, so judicial recourse does not reach it.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI discrimination protections, no legal gender recognition, unregistrable LGBTI organisations; no maximum term given for illicit intercourse and no named criminalising statute identified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented; no ombuds, tribunal, or documented relief appears anywhere in the dossier.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse means any exposure at entry, in care, or in custody resolves without institutional check.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra's register excludes and humiliates but brings no criminal charge and no custody. Here gender nonconformity itself is de-facto criminalised with imprisonment up to five years and no appeal route, so discovery carries custodial severity, not just exclusion.

Close to 0.25-A: both combine criminalisation of presentation with detention/fines, imprisonment rare-to-possible, execution not imposed, inconsistent enforcement and pending reform uncertainty. This dossier adds territorial militia killings but they are dated and outside the courts, roughly offsetting Varnalia's raids on a support centre.

Higher than 0.15-B: Saruth documents repeated border detentions, assaults in custody, delayed habeas and retaliation against complainants — an operating hostile custody pipeline. This dossier documents no current visitor detention record, no custodial abuse claims against state officers, and no credible execution pathway for gender expression.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is a criminal statute regime plus a moral-authority regime plus, in some territories, an armed-group regime. The traveller's everyday exposure runs through the morality provisions: any discovery — document mismatch, seeking care, being seen to have transitioned — converts into exposure to up to five years' imprisonment, with no discrimination protection, no recognition procedure, and no registrable civil society to appeal to. Religious rulings tighten the care axis and align institutions against the traveller rather than shielding them. The militia killings are the most severe documented facts but are a decade old, territorial, and non-judicial; they raise the floor rather than dominate. Nothing documents a working remedy anywhere, so paper silence cannot be read as safety.
